name: perf-budget
filed_under: research/results/h2-* only because research/tests/test_prereg.py maps every MANIFEST file to one hypothesis's results glob; the result is descriptive and decides no hypothesis, as card R4 filed its crosswalk under h1-* with hypothesis none (docs/tasks/backlog.md, row "A results glob outside the hypotheses")

write.why: an allowed write lands one item; the bare equivalent is one row inserted and committed on the same disk

write-deny.why: a denied write records exactly one row, its deny event, appended and committed in one transaction; the bare equivalent of recording one row durably is the same single-row insert, so the ratio is what the gate adds to the event's own write

read.why: a read returns the ten items holding the word in the reader's scopes; the bare equivalent is one SELECT of those rows

budget.name: read-1000
budget.why: a governed read of ten items from a store of 1,000 within 50 ms at p99, on the fake, so the plane's own cost stays a small share of a model turn

budget.name: write-1000
budget.why: an allowed write into a store of 1,000 within 50 ms at p99, on the fake

budget.name: read-10000
budget.why: a governed read from a store of 10,000 within 100 ms at p99, on the fake: the target for a team-sized store, and within 100 times the bare node:sqlite baseline's p99 at the same size

budget.name: write-10000
budget.why: an allowed write into a store of 10,000 within 100 ms at p99, on the fake, and within 100 times the bare node:sqlite baseline's p99 at the same size

notes: Measured once on the machine named in `machine`, while about ten other coding agents ran builds and tests on it: the percentiles are an upper bound on this machine's quiet figures, and are never compared across machines.

Each cell's timed calls follow `suite.warmup` untimed ones; `n` is the number of timed calls. Where n is below 1,000 the p99.9 is interpolated between the two largest samples and is not a resolved tail; where n is below 100 the same holds for the p99.

The store of each size is written through the Plane under preset medium, as user-sourced semantic items in team scopes of at most 1,000 items, so no scope passes any preset's team budget; each preset's plane is then timed over that log and store. The log is a SQLite file in WAL mode in the temporary folder; the baseline is a bare node:sqlite file with the same pragmas, so the fsync of each commit is in both.

100,000 items is not measured: every Plane call here costs time linear in the projection (docs/log/2026-11-21-x15-finding-linear-projection-scans.md), so writing the store one item at a time through the Plane is quadratic: 10,000 items took 664 seconds on the fake (`population` below), and 100,000 would take on the order of 18 hours.

The files adapter is not measured at 10,000 items: its search reads every file in the folder on each read (docs/log/2026-11-21-x15-finding-files-search-linear.md), a median of 0.9 to 1.5 seconds per read at 1,000 items here, so the cell at 10,000 items would take roughly ten seconds a read, several minutes per preset after a population of several minutes more.
